cues.en: I grew up in a car-infested city called London, London, Ontario, Canada. But we don't want to raise our kids in an environment like this, and we move to Amsterdam instead. So why is that? One thing you immediately notice when coming to the Netherlands is that there are a lot of children around. You'll routinely see even young children cycling to school, playing with their friends, and just hanging out in the city.
cues.zh: 我在一个被汽车包围的城市长大，叫伦敦——加拿大安大略省的伦敦。但我们不想在这样的环境里养孩子，于是搬到了阿姆斯特丹。为什么呢？来到荷兰，你立刻会注意到的一件事，就是周围有很多孩子。你会经常看到，甚至很小的孩子也骑车上学、和朋友玩、就在城市里闲逛。

cues.en: The Dutch are famous for having the happiest kids in the world and a big part of that is the fact that they can literally have chocolate sprinkles for breakfast. But the other big factor is the level of independence that children have here. I got used to seeing children everywhere so it was amazing to see the difference the first time I returned to my hometown in Canada. I drove around several residential neighborhoods and while I occasionally saw some kids in the park with their parents, I never saw any children out on their own and
cues.zh: 荷兰人以拥有世界上最快乐的孩子而闻名，很大一部分原因是他们早餐真的可以吃巧克力碎。但另一个重要因素，是这里孩子的独立程度。我习惯了到处都能看到孩子，所以第一次回到加拿大老家时，看到这种差异让我很惊讶。我开车转了几个住宅区，虽然偶尔看到一些孩子和父母在公园里，但我从没看到任何孩子独自在外面，而且

cues.en: That's really sad. I've talked to some parents from suburban Canada about why they don't let their children out on their own and they usually say it's because it's too dangerous. One person even said somebody could come along with a white van, scoop them up and nobody would even notice. Now that's insane because Canada is one of the safest countries in the world and abductions by strangers are exceedingly unlikely. So why do people think this?
cues.zh: 这真的很可悲。我和一些加拿大郊区的父母聊过，问他们为什么不让孩子独自出门，他们通常说因为太危险了。甚至有人说，可能会有人开着白色面包车过来，把孩子抓走，都没人会注意到。这太离谱了，因为加拿大是世界上最安全的国家之一，陌生人绑架的可能性极低。那为什么人们会这么想呢？

cues.en: Well, there are various reasons for this cultural change, including an increase in fear-mongering media, but this is an urban planning channel, so we're going to talk about the reasons linked to city design, because there are a lot of them. In her famous book, The Death and Life of Great American Cities, Jane Jacobs refers to an effect she calls, eyes on the street. Essentially, it means that people feel safer to be in places with many other people, like here, in this suburb of Amsterdam. By comparison,
cues.zh: 这种文化变化有多种原因，包括制造恐慌的媒体增多，但这是一个城市规划频道，所以我们要谈谈与城市设计有关的原因，因为这类原因有很多。Jane Jacobs 在她著名的《美国大城市的死与生》中，提到了一个她称为“街道眼”的效应。本质上，它意味着人们在有很多其他人的地方会感到更安全，比如这里，阿姆斯特丹的这个郊区。相比之下，

cues.en: North American style car-dependent suburbia is desolate for people outside of a car. It's depressing to walk there, and I know, because I've done it a lot in the process of filming these videos. I'm almost always the only one out walking, and I definitely get the feeling that if something happened to me, hundreds of people would drive by without even noticing. So it shouldn't be too surprising that some parents are uncomfortable having their children walk in an environment like this.
cues.zh: 北美那种依赖汽车的郊区，对车外的人来说很荒凉。在那里走路很压抑，我知道，因为我在拍这些视频时经常这么做。我几乎总是唯一一个在外面走路的人，而且我真切地觉得，如果我出了什么事，几百个人开车经过都不会注意到。所以，有些父母不愿意让孩子在这样的环境里走路，也不该太令人意外。

cues.en: Now, there's another safety reason that's a bit more rational. Canadian and American cities are really dangerous for pedestrians. While overall traffic fatalities and develop nations have generally fallen steadily since the 1970s, in the US and Canada, a big part of this was achieved by putting almost everyone inside of a car. But while people inside of cars may be safer, pedestrian deaths have increased significantly in the past few decades due to an increase in car traffic,
cues.zh: 现在，还有另一个稍微更理性的安全原因。加拿大和美国的城市对行人来说真的很危险。虽然自1970年代以来，发达国家的总体交通死亡人数普遍稳步下降，但在美国和加拿大，很大一部分是通过把几乎所有人都放进车里实现的。不过，虽然车里的人可能更安全，但由于汽车交通量增加，过去几十年里行人死亡人数大幅上升，

cues.en: larger trucks and SUVs, distracted driving, and higher vehicle speeds. Ultimately, these unsafe roads lead to a vicious circle. Parents are more likely to drive their children everywhere because it's not safe due to all the cars. But in doing so, they're adding one more car to the problem and making it even less safe. I'd like to point out that this is a unique problem caused only by cars. I mean, nobody ever kept their kids from walking to school just because too many people took the tram.
cues.zh: 更大的卡车和SUV、分心驾驶，以及更高的车速。最终，这些不安全的道路导致恶性循环。父母更可能开车送孩子去任何地方，因为车太多不安全。但这样做，他们又给问题增加了一辆车，让道路更加不安全。我想指出，这是一个只由汽车造成的独特问题。我的意思是，从来没有人因为坐电车的人太多，就不让孩子走路去上学。

cues.en: But also, it's impractical for children to go anywhere on their own in a place like this. Suburbia is car-dependent. That means it's almost impossible to get anywhere without a car. So even if you wanted your child to walk somewhere, they simply can't. It's either too far, or it's not feasible because of a lack of sidewalks. When I have discussions with people from my suburban hellscape of a hometown, they usually agree that the city is quiet
cues.zh: 而且，在这种地方，小孩子根本不可能自己出门去哪儿。郊区严重依赖汽车。这意味着没有车你几乎寸步难行。所以就算你想让孩子步行去哪儿，他们也根本做不到。要么距离太远，要么因为缺少人行道而根本行不通。当我和老家那个宛如地狱般的郊区邻居们聊起时，他们通常也承认那地方虽然安静

cues.en: and soul-crushingly boring, but they will inevitably say, but it's a good place to raise children. I completely disagree. Suburbia may be a good place to shelter toddlers, but as soon as a child is more than about six years old, being trapped in a McMansion on the edge of town seriously inhibits their growth and independence. They might be able to walk to a friend's house if they're lucky enough to live somewhere with a sidewalk, but they're unlikely to be able to walk to school or...
cues.zh: 却无聊得要命，但他们总会补上一句：“不过这里很适合养娃。”我完全不同意。郊区或许适合庇护幼儿，可一旦孩子超过六岁，被困在城郊的 McMansion 里，就会严重阻碍他们的成长和独立性。如果运气好住处附近有人行道，他们或许还能走到朋友家，但基本不可能走着去上学，或者……

cues.en: anywhere else for that matter. In the Netherlands, 60% of children walk or cycle to school compared to 28% in Canada, mostly those kids who live in the few remaining walkable pre-war neighbourhoods that would be illegal to build today due to modern zoning. But when I was a kid, that number was 58% in Canada, almost identical to the Netherlands today. Look at these Canadian kids walking through their rural school in the 1920s.
cues.zh: 去其他任何地方。在荷兰，有 60% 的孩子步行或骑车上学，而加拿大只有 28%，这其中大部分还是住在少数尚存的、适合步行的战前社区里的孩子——而受限于现代分区规划，这类社区如今根本无法合法新建了。但在我小时候，加拿大的这个比例是 58%，跟如今的荷兰几乎一样。看看这些 1920 年代的加拿大孩子走路上乡村学校的情景：

cues.en: through the snow, uphill both ways. Yeah, that never happens anymore. This is the bicycle parking lot of a typical middle school in Amsterdam. And this is the bicycle parking lot of an elementary school. It is obvious here that the majority of children arrive on their own bicycles. I'm constantly hearing excuses from North Americans as to why kids can walk or cycle to school in the Netherlands, but not in Canada. And it's usually some nonsense about the weather or the hills.
cues.zh: 顶风冒雪，来回都是爬坡。是啊，现在再也见不到这种景象了。这是阿姆斯特丹一所普通中学的自行车停车场。这是小学的自行车停车场。很显然，绝大多数孩子都是自己骑车来的。我总听到北美人在找借口，解释为什么荷兰孩子能走路上学或骑车上学，而加拿大就不行。他们常说的无非是天气或坡道之类的借口。

cues.en: Do either of these things explain the massive drop in the number of kids walking to school in Canada? Did Canada's weather get worse in the past 40 years? Did the hills get higher? No, of course not. But we did stop building family-friendly housing anywhere that wasn't car-dependent. Meanwhile, here in the Netherlands, it's not just kids in cities who cycle to school, it's everywhere.
cues.zh: 但这俩原因能解释为什么加拿大走路上学的孩子断崖式减少吗？过去 40 年里加拿大的天气变差了吗？山坡变高了吗？当然没有。但我们确实停止了在非汽车依赖区建造适合家庭居住的房屋。与此同时，在荷兰，不仅是城市里的孩子骑车上学，而是到处都如此。

cues.en: Bicycle Dutch has several videos showing dozens of children cycling long distances to school in suburbs, towns, and villages. And it's more than just school, too. Kids have lots of sports and other activities, so in the Netherlands it's very common to see children walking or cycling while dressed in football gear. Not that kind of football. Or hockey gear. Not that kind of hockey. Because they traveled all these activities by themselves.
cues.zh: Bicycle Dutch 发过好几个视频，展示在郊区、城镇和乡村，几十个孩子长途骑行去上学。而且不仅仅是上学。孩子们有很多体育和其他活动，所以在荷兰经常能看到穿着足球装备步行或骑车的小孩——不是美式橄榄球；或是曲棍球装备——不是冰球那种。因为他们去参加所有这些活动，全都是自己出行。

cues.en: In the US and Canada, you have the stereotype of the suburban soccer mom, the mother who spends all of her time shuttling her kids around from school to activities to play dates and back. Because until a kid is about 16 years old and has their own driver's license, they need to be driven around everywhere by their parents. And this is considered normal. Is it any surprise that kids in the US and Canada don't get enough exercise?
cues.zh: 在美加两国，人们对郊区的“足球妈妈”有一种刻板印象——母亲整天把时间花在接送孩子上学、参加活动、聚会玩耍和回家之间。因为在孩子16岁左右拿到驾照之前，去哪儿都得靠父母开车接送。这还被认为是正常的。美加的孩子运动量不足，这很奇怪吗？

cues.en: I can't blame them for wanting to stay inside playing video games all day when outside looks like this. These problems originate in car-dependent suburbs, but unfortunately, decades of suburbanization have changed the overall culture where now many Canadians don't believe it's safe for any children to be out on their own. So even if you could afford to live in one of the very few remaining walkable neighbourhoods, you still can't give your children the independence they deserve. For example, here in Amsterdam,
cues.zh: 外面要是长这样，我完全理解他们为什么宁愿整天待在屋里打游戏。这些问题源于高度依赖汽车的郊区，但遗憾的是，数十年的郊区化已经改变了整体文化，如今许多加拿大人认为孩子独自出门根本不安全。所以，就算你住得起极少数仅存的适合步行的社区，你依然无法给予孩子应得的独立性。比如，在阿姆斯特丹这里，

cues.en: We started allowing our children to go to the park without us when they were nine and six years old. This is totally normal and accepted in the Netherlands. If we let our children do this in Canada, we would literally have someone call the police. Or worse. Now, you might think I'm exaggerating, but there are stories about this happening all over the US and Canada. And the one that angered me the most was the story of Adrian Crook. Adrian is a father of five children and lives in downtown Vancouver, Canada.
cues.zh: 我们的孩子在九岁和六岁的时候，我们就开始让他们单独去公园了。这在荷兰完全正常且被广泛接受。如果我们在加拿大这么做，真的会有人报警。甚至更糟。你可能会觉得我在夸大其词，但这类事情在美加各地屡见不鲜。其中最让我气愤的是 Adrian Crook 的故事。Adrian 是五个孩子的父亲，住在加拿大温哥华市中心。

cues.en: He has always been a vocal advocate of allowing kids to have their independence and has written about how walkable urban city design makes this easier and more practical. As part of this effort, Adrian and his kids would ride the bus to school every day. He did this with them for two years, but in 2017, he started letting them do it on their own. A short time later, he was anonymously reported to the Ministry of Children and Family Development. The whole story is available on his blog that I'll link to below, but in the end,
cues.zh: 他一直极力倡导给予孩子独立性，并撰文阐述步行友好的城市设计如何让这一切更轻松、更可行。作为践行的一部分，Adrian 每天都会带孩子们坐公交车上学。他陪着孩子们坐了两年，但在2017年，他开始让他们自己坐车。不久后，他就被匿名举报到了儿童与家庭发展部。整个故事都在他的博客里，我会把链接放在下面，但最终的结果是，

cues.en: the Ministry decided that children under the age of 10 could not be unsupervised in or outside of the home for any amount of time. And if Adrian let any of his children out unsupervised again, even to go to the store across the street, his children would be taken away from him. Adrian literally had to spend three years of his life suing the Ministry of Children and Family Development just to allow his children to have some independence. And if you think that's insane, in Ontario, the province where I'm from,
cues.zh: 该部门判定，10岁以下的孩子无论在家里还是室外，任何时候都不能脱离监护。如果 Adrian 再次让任何一个孩子在无人监护的情况下外出，哪怕只是去街对面的商店，他的孩子就会被强行带走。Adrian 真的不得不花了整整三年时间起诉儿童与家庭发展部，只为了能让孩子拥有一些独立性。如果你觉得这很荒谬，那么在我老家安大略省，

cues.en: Children legally cannot be on their own until they're 16 unless, quote, adequate supervision is provided. When I was a kid, adequate supervision was, say, having the phone number of a neighbor. But the problem is, what constitutes adequate supervision is becoming increasingly strict and arbitrarily applied. This article has examples from all over Canada, where child welfare investigations were started because, for example,
cues.zh: 法律规定孩子在16岁之前都不能独处，除非“提供了充分的监护”。在我小时候，“充分的监护”可能就是留个邻居的电话号码。但问题是，什么才算“充分的监护”，界定变得越来越严苛且随意。这篇文章列举了来自加拿大各地的案例，展开儿童福利调查的原因居然包括，比如，

cues.en: A nine-year-old walked to school on her own. Or because a mother allowed her children to play in the fenced backyard of their own house while she was watching them from inside. Now you might say that these visits from police or social workers are just overreactions and it's better to be safe than sorry. But these social workers have the power to literally take your children away from you. You're crazy if you don't think this has a chilling effect that ultimately limits the independence of children in North America.
cues.zh: 一个九岁的孩子独自步行上学；或者一位母亲让孩子在自家带围栏的后院玩耍，自己只是在屋里看着。你可能会说警察或社工上门只是反应过度，小心点总没错。但这些社工可真有权力把你孩子带走。要是你觉得这不会产生寒蝉效应、最终扼杀北美孩子的独立性，那才真是疯了。

cues.en: Personally, I have absolutely no interest in finding out the hard way what the currently accepted definition of adequate supervision may be when it comes to keeping custody of my children. Unfortunately, the solutions to these problems are not easy because they involve changing not just cultural issues, but also the fundamental design of North American cities and suburbs. Traditional mixed-use walkable neighborhoods have a multitude of benefits, but walkability is nearly impossible to retrofit
cues.zh: 就我个人而言，我可一点都不想用惨痛的代价去试探，在保住孩子抚养权的前提下，当下被认可的“充分监护”到底是什么标准。遗憾的是，这些问题并不好解决，因为它们不仅涉及文化观念，还牵扯到北美城市与郊区最根本的设计规划。传统的商住混合、适宜步行的社区有诸多好处，但想要事后补救、改造成适宜步行的环境，

cues.en: on top of car-dependent suburbia. And the last few remaining walkable places in the US and Canada are in such high demand that they're completely unaffordable to most people. Of course, we're also not building any more walkable places like this in Canada because they're illegal to build due to zoning and car-centred regulations like minimum parking requirements. So, what was built 100 years ago is it. We're not getting any more. And if you can't afford it, too bad.
cues.zh: 并硬套在极度依赖汽车的郊区上，几乎是不可能的。而且在美加两国，仅存的几处适合步行的地方需求极高，绝大多数人根本负担不起。当然，我们在加拿大也不会再建这类步行社区了，因为受限于土地规划以及“最低停车配额”这类以汽车为中心的法规，建这些是违法的。所以，100年前建成的就是全部了，以后也不会再有。如果你买不起，那就只能认倒霉。

cues.en: There's this insane myth in North America that when you have kids, you need a car, and you need to live in suburbia when the exact opposite is true. What children really need is fewer cars, because cars are dangerous, especially for children, plus news flash, kids can't drive. But they can walk or cycle, though only if it's safe. Here in the Netherlands, almost all new neighborhoods are walkable, and some of them are even car-free.
cues.zh: 在北美有一种荒谬的迷思，认为只要有了孩子，就必须买车、必须搬去郊区住，但事实恰恰相反。孩子们真正需要的是更少的汽车，因为汽车很危险，对孩子来说尤甚，而且别忘了，小孩子根本不会开车。但在安全有保障的前提下，他们可以走路或骑车。在荷兰，几乎所有新社区都适宜步行，有些甚至彻底禁车。

cues.en: Unsurprisingly, you see kids traveling on their own and playing together in the streets. So a few years ago, my wife and I had to make a decision. What kind of life did we want for us, and more importantly, for our children? The solution seemed pretty clear. We moved to the country with the happiest kids in the world. I'd like to take this opportunity to thank my supporters on Patreon who pay me to remake the classics. If you'd like to join them in supporting this channel, visit patreon.com slash...
cues.zh: 不出所料，在这里你能看到孩子们独自出行，在街头结伴玩耍。所以几年前，我和妻子不得不做出一个抉择：我们究竟想为自己，更重要的是为孩子们，选择怎样的生活？答案似乎显而易见。我们搬到了这个拥有全世界最快乐儿童的国家。借此机会，我想感谢 Patreon 上赞助我重制经典视频的各位支持者。如果你也想加入他们来支持本频道，请访问 patreon.com 斜杠……

cues.en: Not just bikes.
cues.zh: Not just bikes。
